items.title: No shared completion definition across the two programmes
items.whyItMatters: Rates move from 41 to 79 percent with the definition alone (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Apply 12 of 16 sessions or 6 of 8 coaching weeks as attendance-equivalent measures, fixed before analysis.

items.title: Confounding by choice of setting
items.whyItMatters: Patients who choose remote differ at referral.
items.opportunity: Adjust for recorded referral factors and report how strong unmeasured confounding would need to be to explain the result.

items.title: Non-starters handled differently
items.whyItMatters: Excluding non-starters from one programme inflates its completion.
items.opportunity: Count every referral that chose a programme in its denominator.

items.title: Groups most likely to drop out
items.whyItMatters: Women, people aged 75 or over and deprived patients drop out of remote programmes more.
items.opportunity: Report completion by sex, age group, deprivation quintile and distance band.

items.title: No outcome beyond completion for non-completers
items.whyItMatters: Six-minute walk distance at the end exists only for completers.
items.opportunity: Report walk distance change for completers descriptively and never as a comparison of programmes.

errorsFound: A scan reply gave a lead's year as a boolean; it is stored as unknown.
reevaluation: A retrospective comparison is defensible only with one definition, full denominators and explicit handling of choice.
summary: Five gaps; definition and confounding are high severity.
